notes:
DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card names family 'ros' and helper RosDriver, but the confirmed entry symbols are legacy OpenAI Gym environments (gym_gazebo2/envs/MARA/mara.py:40 and mara_real.py:27), registered at gym_gazebo2/__init__.py:6-14. A Gymnasium environment does not become a ROS transport driver because its implementation uses ROS 2 internally; a RosDriver has no step/reset interface and would have replaced the primary environment-step control with topic metadata. The package therefore uses the SDK's GymnasiumDriver over the card's first entry symbol gym_gazebo2.envs.MARA:MARAEnv (MARA-v0), with action_space_ref gym_gazebo2/envs/MARA/mara.py:169-172 for the upstream Box(-pi, pi) action space. Backends: only fake=.fake:FakeGymGazebo2 exists; no sim or hardware backend was declared, so the upstream simulator was never constructed or run. The upstream environment needs ROS 2 Dashing, Gazebo 9.9.0 and the MARA workspace (INSTALL.md:17-22); none of that is installed where the gate runs. A live deployment would need an operator-supplied factory that imports the gym_gazebo2 registration (or installs an equivalent entry point) before gym.make('MARA-v0'); this package does not provide or claim that path. NOT COVERED: the upstream MARAEnv was never imported or run; no Gazebo, ROS 2 graph, MARA URDF, KDL chain, controller, physics engine, contact sensor or camera is modelled. The fake is an F0 analytic kinematic stand-in, not a recording, and was never compared with the upstream environment. It returns the full upstream 24-value observation size (not a reduced array), built in the upstream concatenation order (mara.py:272-276), but every observation value, the reset jitter, the integration gain, the reward and the 1024-step limit are placeholder test data marked '# placeholder'. The fake preserves the native legacy API before adaptation: reset() returns one observation, step(action) returns (obs, reward, done, info), seed(seed) returns [seed], and close() exists; the production mhs.bridge.gymnasium adapter, not fake.py, recognizes the four-tuple and observation-only reset. One consequence is recorded in the fidelity gaps: the legacy done flag is adapted by the bridge to terminated=True and truncated=False, while upstream done marks the 1024-step iterator limit, which a Gymnasium environment would normally call truncation. reset(seed) reseeds the fake's placeholder RNG only; upstream reset restores the Gazebo simulation. No hardware was attached, no hardware backend exists, and fake evidence establishes no real ROS or hardware run. This package is model-authored and unreviewed: driver.lock.json authored_by is the model identity and reviewed_by is null. Safety: simulated R0 (isolated simulation stepping), no native stop; the e-stop is the runtime's latching software control, which refuses new step/reset/seed calls until mhs.safety.reset; no physical device or Gazebo process is stopped. Expected warnings left by the gate and their reasons: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (the bridge buffers the seed for the next reset and makes no native call), and G8.NO_UNIT x4 for ticks, the reset seed, the seed-class seed and action.values (simulator inputs with no catalogue unit; the upstream code states the action bounds but no unit, so no unit is invented). There were no G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warnings. test_driver.py keeps the check_driver call and adds ten repository-specific cases on the fake backend; all passed. The clone at 545e203e07895927fd7aae66596d83d97ee89fe5 was read only and stays unmodified.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked the card deviation, every fact, action_space_ref, the fake and the stop text against mara.py, mara_real.py, ut_mara.py and ut_launch.py at the pin. The GymnasiumDriver deviation is right (MARA-v0 is a legacy gym.Env whose ROS 2 topics are internal transport), but the fact on done cited only the 1024 default, the fact that MARAReal-v0 implements no arm I/O was wrong (MARARealEnv publishes JointTrajectory commands to a real arm on /mara_controller/command), the safe_state said the simulator stops advancing although live Gazebo keeps running, and the fake integrated actions as deltas although upstream sends absolute joint-position targets. Reviewer changed driver.py (three facts corrected, six source facts added, safe_state, five fidelity gaps), fake.py (placeholder tracking toward the commanded position, the upstream == done rule), test_driver.py (one case now asserts absolute-target semantics instead of 'the zero action changes no joint') and facts.md, and regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json. The gate and collect.py --strict pass with the expected G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL (seed buffered for the next reset) and G8.NO_UNIT warnings and the digest unchanged. For the human reviewer: Fake-only contract; no sim backend is declared. The stock path gym.make('MARA-v0') would construct MARAEnv inside the server process: it parses the server's command line (argparse can raise SystemExit), launches Gazebo, calls rclpy.init and waits without timeouts for /spawn_entity, /reset_simulation and controller states, and close() kills the launch process tree and calls rclpy.shutdown; a live deployment needs an owned, isolated factory. The software latch neither pauses Gazebo nor stops the last trajectory. MARAReal-v0 commands a real MARA arm and is not covered; a package for it is a robot arm at R2 or above with an acknowledged stop. The card's override still names family ros and MARARealEnv; the proposal above drops both.

MODEL REVIEW (grok-4.7, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Item 12 repair. MARAEnv publishes JointTrajectory on /mara_controller/command (mara.py:99 and 149). Evidence is contract_checked on the fake only. reviewed_by stays null.
